answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is severe and non-negotiable. Memory_c4 demonstrates that renegotiation at renewal recovered real margin and moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms—directly applicable to this scenario. Memory_c2 shows that switching to a low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, but that is a higher-risk move given the 94% line utilization and 14-day window with no auto-renewal. Verification of c4 will confirm whether aggressive renegotiation can bridge the 18% gap; verification of c2 will confirm the switching path as a credible fallback if negotiation fails. Negotiating_terms is the highest-probability play: (1) it preserves the incumbent's integration stability (memory_c1), (2) it leverages proven renegotiation success (memory_c4), (3) it avoids migration risk during a critical utilization period, and (4) it buys time to evaluate add_second_source or deferred renewal in the next cycle. Multi-year commitment unlocking (memory_c6) could be layered into the negotiation. If the incumbent cannot hit 18% reduction through renegotiation, the verified fallback of switching (memory_c2) remains executable within the 14-day window, but carries higher delivery risk. This approach preserves optionality while minimizing immediate disruption risk.
